metadata.title: What is ARIA?
metadata.subtitle: Roles, Properties & States
metadata.description: ARIA lets you influence the accessibility tree directly — but only use it when native HTML isn't enough.

rules.label: Don't use ARIA if you don't have to
rules.good: Native HTML handles roles, states, and keyboard for free
rules.bad: ARIA adds semantics only — not behavior or keyboard support

rules.label: Use role to define what an element is
rules.good: Screen reader announces element type correctly
rules.bad: Generic div/span with no semantic meaning
rules.code:
// ✓ Custom listbox — role tells SR what this is
  • Option A
  • Option B
// ✓ Custom dialog

Confirm action

rules.label: Use aria-label or aria-labelledby to name elements
rules.good: SR announces a meaningful name for the control
rules.code:
// ✓ Icon button with aria-label // ✓ aria-labelledby points to visible text

Recent Activity

rules.label: Use aria-describedby to attach hints and errors
rules.good: Hint text is read after the label when the field is focused
rules.bad: Hint is visible but completely ignored by assistive tech
rules.code: Must be at least 8 characters.

rules.label: Keep aria state in sync with visual state
rules.good: SR announces the correct current state on every change
rules.bad: aria-expanded stays 'false' while the menu is visually open
rules.code:
const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
    ...

rules.label: Use aria-live for dynamic content updates
rules.good: Screen reader announces the change without user navigating to it
rules.bad: UI updates silently — screen reader user has no idea

rules.label: Never use aria-hidden on focusable elements
rules.good: Hidden decorative elements are skipped by SR without blocking keyboard
rules.bad: aria-hidden on a focusable element creates a keyboard trap

checklist.item: Prefer native HTML elements over ARIA whenever possible
role defines what the element is to assistive technology
aria-label / aria-labelledby gives every interactive element an accessible name
aria-describedby links hints, instructions, and errors to their input
aria-expanded, aria-checked, aria-selected stay in sync with visual state
aria-live regions announce dynamic content changes
aria-hidden never applied to focusable elements
Custom widgets implement full keyboard interaction (arrow keys, Enter, Escape)
ARIA does not add behavior — keyboard handlers must be coded manually
